title: Meter ingest API
summary: Send usage events over HTTPS one at a time or in batches of 5,000. Every event carries an idempotency key, so a retry never bills twice.
body:
The ingest API accepts JSON events with a meter name, a customer reference, a timestamp, a quantity and any dimensions you want to price or report on later. Batches are accepted atomically: all events in a batch are recorded, or none are.

Retries are safe. Abacene keeps every idempotency key for 35 days (story figure) and drops duplicates before aggregation, then shows how many it dropped on the invoice explain tree.

Built for bursty traffic

Ingest is decoupled from rating. A spike of 200,000 events per second queues, it doesn't drop. Aggregates catch up within a minute at p99 in the story benchmarks.
spec: Batch size: 5,000 events|p99 ingest: 41 ms|Idempotency window: 35 days|Max dimensions: 16 per event

title: Late and duplicate events
tagline: The window is a setting, not a surprise
summary: Events that arrive late re-rate the open period. After the window closes they post as an adjustment on the next invoice, never a silent rewrite.
body:
Usage arrives late for ordinary reasons: a mobile client offline overnight, a queue backlog, a partner who sends files daily. Abacene holds each billing period open for a late-event window (72 hours by default) and re-rates it as events land.

After the window, a closed invoice is never changed. Late events become a dated adjustment line on the next invoice, with its own explain tree.
spec: Default window: 72 hours|Max window: 30 days|Closed invoices: immutable|Adjustments: itemized

title: Dimensions and aggregation
tagline: Group by what you price on
summary: Roll events up by customer, meter and any dimension — region, model, plan — using sum, count, max or unique counts.
body:
A meter defines how raw events become billable quantities: sum(quantity), count(), max(quantity) over the period, or unique(device_id) for active-device pricing.

Dimensions you send on events can be used to split a line (per region, per model) or to price differently (a premium model at a higher rate) without creating new meters.
spec: Aggregations: sum, count, max, unique|Grain: hourly roll-ups|Backfill: up to 13 months|Query API: yes

title: Rate cards and pricing models
summary: Per-unit, graduated tiers, volume tiers, packages, minimums and caps — in rate cards that are versioned, so an old invoice always re-renders the same way.
body:
A rate card is a versioned price book attached to a plan or a single customer contract. Changing a price creates a new version with an effective date; invoices remember the version they were rated with.

Models

ModelExample
Per unit$0.40 per 1,000 lookups
Graduated tiersFirst 10M at $0.03 / 1k, next 40M at $0.025 / 1k
Volume tiersAll units at the rate of the tier you land in
Package$106 per block of 1M tiles
Minimum / cap$500 monthly minimum, $20,000 cap

title: Prepaid credits and burndown
summary: Sell prepaid credit blocks or annual commitments. Usage draws them down in order, with alerts at thresholds you set and a burndown on every invoice.
body:
Credits are a ledger of their own: granted, consumed, expired. Usage rated in a period consumes credits oldest-first (or by priority you set), and the remaining balance is printed on every invoice and in the customer usage page.

Alerts fire at 50%, 80% and 100% consumption by default and go to webhooks or email, so account managers hear about renewals before the customer is surprised.
spec: Order: oldest first or priority|Expiry: per grant|Alerts: 50 / 80 / 100 %|Rollover: optional

title: Invoice explain
summary: Open any invoice line and walk it back: rate card version, aggregate, dimension split, events received, duplicates dropped and late events counted.
body:
Invoice explain is the reason support teams adopt Abacene. When a customer disputes a line, the answer is a tree, not a spreadsheet export and an afternoon of SQL.

The same tree is available in the API and as CSV or JSON export, so your own billing page or your auditors can use it.

What the tree shows

  • Price: rate card name, version and model
  • Aggregate: the quantity and how it was computed
  • Dimensions: the split behind the quantity
  • Events: received, duplicates dropped, late events counted, first and last timestamps
  • Ledger: the journal entry the line posted to
spec: Depth: line → event counts|API: GET /v1/invoices/{id}/explain|Export: CSV, JSON|Retention: life of account

title: Reconciliation and ledger export
summary: Each invoice posts journal entries you can export to your accounting system, with a reconciliation report that ties usage, invoices and payments together.
body:
At month end, Abacene produces a reconciliation report: usage rated, invoices issued, credits consumed, adjustments posted. Totals tie to the journal entries exported to your accounting system as CSV or over SFTP.

Payments are matched by reference from your payment processor export. Unmatched items appear on a short list instead of a long spreadsheet.
spec: Journal export: CSV, SFTP|Report: monthly + on demand|Payment match: by reference|Audit log: every change

title: Usage pages for your customers
tagline: Fewer “why is my bill high” tickets
summary: A hosted, branded usage page per customer with current-period usage, credit balance and the explain tree for every past invoice line.
body:
Give every customer a link to their own usage: current period by meter and dimension, the projected invoice, credit balance and past invoices with explain trees. You choose which meters and dimensions are visible.

Pages are server-rendered and work without JavaScript. Access is by signed link or your own SSO.
spec: Branding: logo + colors|Access: signed link or SSO|Projection: current period|Embeds: none required
